release.excerpt: O king, bid me not be seated, while Hector is still lying uncared for in your tents, but accept the great ransom which I have brought you, and give him to me at once that I may look upon him. May you prosper with the ransom and reach your own land in safety, seeing that you have suffered me to live and to look upon the light of the sun.” Achilles looked at him sternly and said, “Vex me, sir, no longer; I am of myself minded to give up the body of Hector.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Priam enters the enemy camp to ransom Hector’s body. He asks Achilles to remember his own father. The two men mourn, and Achilles agrees to release the body and allow time for burial.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “others looked one to another and marvelled also, but Priam besought Achilles saying, “Think of your father, O Achilles like unto the gods, who is such even as I am, on the sad threshold of old age. It may be that those who dwell near him harass him, and there is none to keep war and ruin from him. Yet”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Priam asks Achilles to accept a ransom and return Hector's body. Achilles says he is already minded to give it up.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Notice the limit of the encounter: Priam recovers a body, not a living son, and the war has not ended. Compassion interrupts vengeance without undoing its losses.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: The final model is hard restraint: seeing an enemy as human when violence would be easier.

quiz.prompt: What does Priam ask Achilles to return?

quiz.prompt: Why does Priam mention Achilles’ father?

choices.text: He claims Achilles’ father ordered Hector’s death.
He offers Achilles a new military alliance.
He appeals to a shared vulnerability across enemy lines.
